schemes.name: comp20_fanned_bar_corner_hinge
schemes.secondary_language: a bar is bent at one corner hinge so its two halves fan out, the opening angle generating a tapered outdoor wedge rather than a straight street edge
schemes.formal_principle: 하나의 바가 한쪽 모서리를 경첩으로 두 팔을 벌려, 그 사이에 쐐기 모양의 외부 공간을 조각한다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: two arms fanning from a corner hinge
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the corner hinge is a different spatial logic from the diagonal fracture (comp19: bar breaks at midspan); here the hinge is fixed and the two arms radiate — the outdoor wedge is the subject, not a residual gap

ops.why: half the plot length at full height budget with chamfered corners — the bar is the base that will be bent; chamfer keeps the hinge corner legible as a pivot rather than a squared junction

a single planar cut at 22 degrees from the long axis creates the hinge; slot 0 keeps the pieces in contact at the apex corner while the open end fans out — the two arms remain in structural contact at the pivot
one arm is slid laterally so the wedge opens on the cross side; the stagger preserves the hinge contact at the narrow end while widening the outdoor room at the far end
the inner face of the wider arm is carved back at entry level so the arrival enters the wedge rather than reading the face of the bar — the civic approach is through the fanned opening, not around it

schemes.name: comp20_shear_stack_alternating_plan_offset
schemes.secondary_language: four bands are stacked and each band is sheared in the plan direction opposite to the one below, so the silhouette shifts left and right alternately as it rises
schemes.formal_principle: 네 켜의 밴드가 쌓이며 한 켜씩 좌우로 반대 방향으로 평면이 밀려, 입면이 지그재그로 오르내린다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a left-right alternating plan shear as it rises
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the alternation is in plan (shear, not section cantilever), which differs from the alternating cantilever in section (comp19); four sheared bands also differ from the kite-plan turning tower (O49) which rotates rather than translates

ops.why: four bands on the narrow axis at near-full height; contrast 1.15 keeps each band's footprint close to the one below so the shear reads as offset rather than taper — a lower contrast would make the stack read as ziggurat

the top band is sheared 14 degrees along the long face toward the street; the angle is within the 5-45 range and is shallow enough that the floor plates remain usable — the limitation is that all four bands receive the same angle declaration

alternating bands are offset toward the back face to complete the left-right pattern; the stagger operates on the same split-band body so its direction alternates with the shear to produce the visible zigzag

a notch is cut from the street face at the base band so the ground-level entry is recessed under the first offset overhang — the carve makes the alternating offset legible from the street by framing an entry beneath the first shift

schemes.name: comp20_interlocked_cross_bars
schemes.secondary_language: two bars cross at right angles and interlock through each other at different floor levels, the bite zone becoming a shared double-height room
schemes.formal_principle: 두 바가 직각으로 교차하며 서로 다른 층 높이에서 맞물려, 물린 구역이 두 켜 높이의 공유 공간이 된다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: two bars crossing and biting through each other
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the interlock differs from the bridge-pair (comp19_08) because the bars physically cross rather than run in parallel; the bite zone is the spatial content, not the gap between them

ops.why: a quarter of the plot length at full height — one bar whose short dimension will be the bite depth for the crossing bar; the footprint is narrow enough that the cross bar remains visibly wider

a second bar crosses at 42% bite depth and 55% of the seed plan size; reach 0.35 is within the 0-1 allowed range and places the bite zone offset from centre so the two arms of the crossing bar are unequal — the longer arm reads as the approach wing and the shorter as the service end; the limitation is that floor plate efficiency at the bite zone requires verification against the 2.4m minimum room depth
the end of the longer crossing arm is carved to open the principal entry; the carve recesses the face under the bite and marks the moment where the interlock is visible from the street approach

schemes.name: comp20_cross_void_four_residual_quadrants
schemes.secondary_language: a full-coverage block is carved with two perpendicular through-cuts, the cuts producing a cross-shaped public void and four discrete occupied quadrants at its corners
schemes.formal_principle: 꽉 찬 매스에 두 개의 직교 관통 절개가 십자형 공공 공간을 만들고, 네 모서리의 점유 덩어리가 그 교차로를 둘러싼다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a cross-void organizing four corner masses
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the cross void is the positive spatial content while the four corner masses are the built elements — this differs from the four equal halls inside a frame (O36) which has an outer enclosing wall, and from the radial wings (comp19_11) which have no outer perimeter

ops.why: the full parcel at 82% of the height budget — a compact medium-height block that is BCR-limited; the remaining height reserves room for the cross void to be read against a clear sky rather than compressed by a taller solid
a through-cut from the street face at 32% plan width runs the full depth of the block; the 'through' flag makes it a complete passage rather than a recess — the north-south civic route

a second through-cut at 90 degrees from the east face at 28% plan width completes the cross; the two cuts together create the four discrete corner quadrants and the shared centre intersection — the limitation is that each quadrant's floor area depends on both cut sizes and must sum to the required programme

the entry corners of the cross are notched at the parcel boundary to widen the threshold and confirm the arrival at the cross rather than at the face of any single quadrant — the four notches read as four gateways into the shared civic centre

schemes.name: comp20_loop_warped_wings_opposing_slopes
schemes.secondary_language: a four-sided perimeter loop whose two long wings slope in opposite directions, so the roof of one long arm rises toward the court while the other falls away from it
schemes.formal_principle: 사면 루프의 두 긴 날개 지붕이 서로 반대 방향으로 기울어, 한 날개는 마당 쪽으로 오르고 다른 날개는 그 반대로 내려간다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a loop with opposing-slope long wings
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; opposing slopes on the two long wings of a loop differ from the butterfly valley bar (comp19_03) which is a single bar, and from the warped perimeter (O9 descending toward open side) which uses one consistent slope direction; here the two long wings actively contradict each other across the court

ops.why: the parcel-scale four-bar ring at 92% of the height budget; bar 0.24 is deep enough for office rooms on both faces of each wing without narrowing the court excessively
the front long wing (open face) grades downward toward the street so its ridge sinks on the civic approach — the contrast with the back wing rising makes the court read as a ramp-edged room

the back long wing receives a butterfly valley so it descends from both its ends toward a gutter at its centre; the valley is the back wall's signature and contradicts the front wing's grade — the two long wings together produce the opposing-slope reading from inside the court

the street face of the front wing is carved at the entry bay so the arrival passes through the grade rather than reading it end-on; the carve also keeps the front wing's floor area within BCR by removing the deepest point of the low end

schemes.name: comp20_sunken_base_mansard_crown
schemes.secondary_language: a compact block sinks its lower storey into the ground while a mansard crown shoulders upward at the top, maximising the middle floors as the primary office zone
schemes.formal_principle: 콤팩트한 매스의 아래 켜는 지반 아래로 내려가고 위 켜는 맨사드로 솟아올라, 중간 사무 층이 두 극단 사이에 가장 넓게 펼쳐진다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a sunken base with a mansard crown
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the sink-and-crown combination is a section proposition that has no equivalent on the board — sink is used here for the first time in this corpus and mansard is used on a compact block rather than on a tall bar, which is the proper proportional register for the mansard shoulder

ops.why: half the plot at 88% of the height budget — a compact solid whose section will be defined by sinking below and shouldering above; the mid-range height keeps the mansard shoulder visible against the sky rather than lost at maximum height

the base sinks 25% of its own height below grade, creating a semi-basement service and parking level exempt from FAR under 시행령 119조 — the visible building above ground is correspondingly shorter and the street reads the middle office floors as the primary face

the mansard crown shoulders upward at 55% pitch with a 22% shoulder band — on a compact block rather than a tall bar the shoulder width is proportionally narrower and the form reads as a crown rather than a tent; the pitch is steep enough to be legible from the street and the limitation is that the attic zone under the mansard must be verified against the floor-height minimum

the street face is carved at the sunken entry level so the semi-basement entry is recessed and the approach descends a half-flight to the lobby — the carve makes the sink legible at the civic face rather than concealed behind a flat plinth

schemes.name: comp20_z_plan_three_offset_bars
schemes.secondary_language: three bars are arranged in a Z-plan, each offset half its own width from the previous, so the plan reads as a staggered march across the site
schemes.formal_principle: 세 바가 Z자 배치로 각자 절반 너비씩 어긋나 놓여, 평면이 대지를 가로질러 엇갈리며 행진한다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a Z-plan of three staggered parallel bars
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the Z-plan is a plan organization, not a section hierarchy — the bars are at the same height and their spatial content is the two parallel slot-courts between them, which distinguishes this from the slip-pair (O52, two slabs) and from the bridge-pair (comp19_08, perpendicular bars bridged)

ops.why: a quarter of the plot length at 88% of the height budget with a trapezoidal profile — one bar whose wider face will be the outer street front and whose narrower end faces into the slot between bars; the profile gives each bar a directionality that reads in the Z-plan

three bars in a loose grid with no tie plate; spread 1.45 ensures each bar clears 3.9 m from the adjacent bar at the gap gate, creating two parallel slot-courts; tie 0 keeps the courts open; the limitation is that 'pack' places bars in a grid and the Z-offset must be confirmed in the delivered footprint

the middle bar is offset 32% toward the cross face so the three bars read as Z rather than as three parallel identical slots — the stagger is the plan move that creates the Z; without it the three bars would be uniform slots

the street-facing end of each outer bar is carved to open an entry from the long slot-court — the civic approach enters the Z from the street end and traverses both courts rather than arriving at a single face

schemes.name: comp20_vault_spanning_cascading_slabs
schemes.secondary_language: three cascading slabs of decreasing depth are stacked from back to front and a single barrel vault spans all three as a shared roof, so the vault reads as a unified canopy over a stepped section
schemes.formal_principle: 깊이가 줄어드는 세 켜의 슬래브가 앞으로 갈수록 낮아지며 쌓이고, 하나의 배럴 볼트가 그 위를 한 지붕으로 덮어 통합된 계단형 단면을 만든다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a barrel vault as a unified roof over a cascading section
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the vault here is the unifying roof that spans across the cascade rather than a section of a single bar — the cascade is the programme logic and the vault is the formal resolution, which differs from the cascading terrace grade (comp19_05) which is a walkable topography without a roof

ops.why: three slabs aligned to the back with contrast 1.55 so the deepest slab is at ground and the shallowest at the top — the cascade reads front-to-back in section; height 0.85 keeps the stack under the legal storey limit with margin for the vault above

a barrel vault with rise 0.45 and two bays spans the cross direction, covering all three stacked slabs as a single roof; bays 2 gives two vaulted units that match the two-court reading of the cascade — the vault unifies the stepped section under one formal gesture; the limitation is that vault rise is capped at 1.5 storeys so the declared 0.45 delivers a visible arch rather than a flat ceiling

the street face of the lowest slab is carved at the entry bay so the arrival enters under the vault before stepping up through the cascade — the carve makes the vault's interior visible from the street approach

schemes.name: comp20_butterfly_mat_two_courts
schemes.secondary_language: a near-full-coverage mat whose roof is a butterfly valley section has two courts carved from above, one on each descending wing, so daylight enters through the valley and the courts together
schemes.formal_principle: 거의 전면을 덮는 판의 지붕이 V자 골짜기 단면이고, 내려가는 두 날개 위에 마당 하나씩이 파여 있어 골짜기와 마당이 함께 빛을 받아들인다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a butterfly section with a court on each wing
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the butterfly section combined with plan courts is a section-and-plan synthesis not present on the board — the board's inscribed court (comp19_10) is in a flat-topped block, and the butterfly bar (comp19_03) has no courts; here the valley roof and the courts are a single spatial logic where the low points gather both rain and daylight

ops.why: the full parcel at 78% of the height budget — a medium-height mat whose BCR is near-maximum and whose section is the subject rather than its height

the valley ridge runs the long axis at its centreline; pitch 0.42 is a 1:2.4 slope, shallow enough to be structural across a near-full-parcel mat — the two descending wings are each the site of one court

a court is inscribed from the top of the mat on the street-facing wing; depth 0.38 within the 0.1-0.5 range brings the court floor to approximately the second storey level; the valley already collects light at the centreline so the court supplements it with a second daylight source on the lower wing

the second court is carved from the back wing's cross face; this carve-from-the-side differs from the top inscribe and creates an open-sided court on the back wing rather than a contained courtyard — the two courts are spatially distinct, one contained and one open, which is the programme benefit of the butterfly geometry

schemes.name: comp20_wedge_section_one_end_lifted
schemes.secondary_language: a single bar is grounded at its back end and lifted at its street end so it reads as a wedge section in elevation — a long ramp from ground to sky
schemes.formal_principle: 하나의 바가 뒷면은 땅에 닿고 앞면은 들려, 입면 전체가 경사 쐐기 단면으로 읽힌다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a wedge bar grounded at back, lifted at front
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the lift here applies to one end of a bar rather than to a full mat — the result is a wedge section, not a pilotis proposition; this differs from the mat-raised-on-piers (comp19_06) because the element is a bar and the space under the lifted front end is the street threshold rather than a civic hall

ops.why: half the plot depth on the short axis with a trapezoidal profile — the bar's wider end faces the back and its narrower end faces the street; the trapezoidal plan already begins the wedge reading before the lift is declared

the bar is lifted 35% of a storey at its street end, creating the wedge section — clearance 0.35 is within the 0.1-0.4 gate and delivers approximately 1.3 m of clear threshold under the front corner; the grounded back end is the structural bearing and the lifted front is the civic canopy

the underside of the wedge is declared as a ramp so the approach reads the inclined soffit as a directing surface; walk:false keeps it as a visual rather than occupiable slope — the limitation is that grade and lift together must not produce a geometry where the declared clearance is consumed by the ramp angle

the lifted street face is carved back at the thin end so the entry threshold is a deep recess under the wedge rather than a flush face — the carve deepens the canopy and confirms that the wedge's spatial content is the covered approach, not the silhouette

schemes.name: comp20_corner_joint_two_unequal_towers
schemes.secondary_language: a taller and a shorter compact volume share exactly one corner, their two bodies otherwise free-standing, so the joint corner is the only point of contact
schemes.formal_principle: 키가 다른 두 덩어리가 단 하나의 모서리만 공유하며, 그 점 접촉이 두 매스의 유일한 건축적 접합이 된다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: two unequal towers touching at one corner only
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; point-contact at one corner is a spatial condition not present on the board — the two bars bridged (comp19_08) connect with bridges, the extracted socket (comp19_12) is connected with a bridge at mid-height, the aggregate operations spread volumes apart; here the join is minimum possible: one shared corner edge

ops.why: two compact volumes at minimum spread (1.05) so they nearly touch; tie 0 keeps the ground clear; height 1.0 gives the full height budget to both units — they will be differentiated by the operations that follow

the two units are split in height by contrast 1.8 so the taller tower is 80% taller than the short one; gap 0 keeps the corner in contact; the contrast 1.8 is within the 1.2-3.5 allowed range and produces a height difference that reads clearly without being structurally extreme

the taller tower is shifted slightly toward the street so the shared corner reads as a genuine pivot — without the shift both towers would align flat-face to flat-face and the corner contact would be invisible in plan

the shared corner zone is carved at base level on the cross face to create a threshold that acknowledges the point contact — the carve opens a diagonal entry slot that reads the two towers simultaneously and makes the corner junction the address of the building rather than a structural awkwardness

schemes.name: comp20_lodged_bar_across_roof
schemes.secondary_language: a compact host block carries a second bar lodged across its roof, the bar extending equally on both sides beyond the host and reading as a cross in the sky above the civic entry
schemes.formal_principle: 낮은 기단 위로 하나의 바가 지붕을 가로질러 걸쳐지며 양쪽으로 똑같이 내밀어, 하늘 속에 십자로를 그린다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a bar lodged across a podium roof
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the lodge operation places the upper bar across the host roof without embedding it — the cross in the sky is the formal reading and it differs from the two-bridge pair (comp19_08) because one element sits on the roof of the other rather than spanning between two parallel peers

ops.why: half the plot at 55% of the height budget with a stadium profile — a low wide podium whose rounded long faces will be the landing zone for the lodged bar; the stadium profile softens the podium's civic edges and distinguishes its form from the bar above

a bar at 28% of the host width is lodged across the roof at 35% over the host edge, extending on both sides; height 0.52 gives the lodged bar approximately two storeys within the remaining height budget; the lodge places it straddling the podium so the cross reading is immediate in elevation — the limitation is that the bar's structural bearing on the podium roof requires a verified transfer beam, which is not modelled here

the street face of the podium is carved at entry level so the arrival passes under the lodged bar and reads the cross against the sky; the carve deepens the threshold and makes the bar's extension beyond the podium face the first architectural experience of the building

the lodged bar is declared as cantilever-capable toward the cross face so its extension beyond the host reads as a structural statement rather than just a visual overhang; reach 0.28 is the tested delivery limit and keeps the extension within the structural gate; levels 2 confirms the bar has the floor count to act as a genuine cantilever rather than a decorative fin
